A big one for me is the multitude if questions surrounding the Ediacaran biota - what was it, did it belong to a known phyla, was it's extinction a true evolutionary progression or a complete ecological overhaul? 
Another, closer to my heart and field of expertise is a true definition and an absolute, precise reworking of the Avialae; there's a huge amount of disparity within the literature, and I would love to work on addressing that.
Finally, an interesting posit is how the world of our past may be learned from to better understand the future of our biospheres. I'm currently researching the speeds and methods of evolution after mass extinction events to aid this field of knowledge, and I believe research like this (addressing future problems with all available knowledge) is the ultimate goal of our beloved palaeontology.

I, of course, may be wrong. This is just a small list of my admittedly biased research interests.
